original_test_intent: Verify the intended BMC exposes a readable, schema-valid and correct Redfish CertificateService resource and advertised metadata without changing its certificate or trust state.
original_method: Establish an approved TLS bootstrap/trust path, discover CertificateService from the service root, perform a protected read-only GET, validate resource and linked collection/action metadata against the exact firmware contract, redact sensitive details and audit that no action was invoked.
manual_activity: The security owner approves bootstrap/trust and expected exposed metadata, reviews redacted action targets and confirms the no-action boundary.
required_inputs: Exact BMC/firmware/API identity and current certificate fingerprint/chain
Approved CA or documented secure bootstrap procedure for an initial/self-signed certificate
CertificateService schema, linked certificate collections and expected action metadata/parameters
Protected read-only account/session and sensitive-field redaction/retention policy
safety_requirements: Never bypass TLS silently; verify approved CA/fingerprint/bootstrap identity
Keep credentials outside command line/URL/output and use least privilege
Issue GET only; prohibit GenerateCSR, certificate replace/delete/renew and all Actions targets
Do not follow an action link or claim action presence proves functionality
Stop on trust mismatch, wrong BMC, unexpected target, malformed schema or sensitive-data leakage
agent_execution_scope: Verify BMC/TLS/bootstrap identity and discover CertificateService
GET resource with protected authentication and validate schema/required fields
Enumerate/redact certificate collection links and action metadata without invoking them
Audit request methods and compare exposure to the owner contract
Make no certificate mutation or functional-support claim
engineer_actions: Approve trust/bootstrap, expected CertificateService/action metadata and redaction policy
Confirm any OEM action targets/parameters and explicit no-action scope
Review evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED; schedule functional certificate testing separately if needed

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The resource GET is source-aligned, but curl -k/CLI credentials defeat certificate trust and the mention of GenerateCSR risks overstating or crossing the read-only boundary.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use an approved certificate-validating/bootstrap-aware Redfish client to discover and GET CertificateService, schema-check and redact its metadata, and verify by method audit that no action was invoked.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: CertificateService GET, response correctness and 5/5-minute estimates remain; observed Actions are metadata only.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Pin BMC identity and certificate fingerprint/chain before authentication, validate @odata resource/schema and normalize action targets/parameters, then generate a signed no-write audit and redacted metadata hash.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces the paradoxical TLS bypass in a certificate-service check with explicit trust/bootstrap and a machine-verifiable no-action boundary.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Readable JSON or an Actions object proves only exposure; it does not prove GenerateCSR/certificate installation works and must not be reported as such.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Certificate metadata defines the management trust boundary. An accidental POST can invalidate access, while overly broad evidence may disclose security posture; both require owner policy.

project_override_considerations: OEM action names and bootstrap policies may differ. They may be documented as expected metadata but cannot authorize execution of those actions in this row.
expected_evidence: Exact source row/variant/hash and BMC/firmware/API/current-certificate identity
Approved TLS/CA/bootstrap result and protected-session audit
Redacted CertificateService status/JSON/hash and schema/required-field validation
Linked certificate collections plus normalized action targets/parameters compared to owner contract

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require a read of CertificateService. DeepSeek's action-exposure wording is acceptable only as metadata and is explicitly prevented from becoming functional action coverage.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Trust/bootstrap, schema and owner metadata inputs gate execution but do not prevent the static review.

review_improvement: Makes trust validation part of a certificate-service test, distinguishes metadata from function and gives the read-only boundary an auditable form.
independent_technical_reasoning: Using -k while testing CertificateService would accept an untrusted endpoint and make the resource evidence incapable of proving which BMC trust boundary was observed. The current certificate identity must therefore be established before protected authentication, including a controlled bootstrap path when CA trust is not yet deployed. Action metadata can be validated safely as data, but a POST changes security state and represents separate coverage with independent recovery requirements.
